Tags & Masking Policies

Tag catalogs, schemas, tables and columns, then write one masking policy against a tag. Masks are applied at query time to every path that reads data (SQL editor, dashboards, previews, exports, Genie, jobs).

Define a tag
TagAllowed valuesDescriptionObjectsPolicies

A policy masks every column carrying its tag for everyone except the exempt roles/users. Lower priority number wins.

No masking policies yet. Create one to start protecting tagged columns.

A row filter restricts which rows of every table carrying its tag are visible, for everyone except the exempt roles/users. Multiple applicable policies on one table combine: all must pass.

No row filter policies yet. Tag a table, then create one to restrict its rows.
User attributes

The membership table 'attribute' mode policies read: which values a user (or, as a default, a role) is assigned for a key. No assignment means no visible rows.

PrincipalAttributeValues
No attribute assignments yet.
Nothing to suggest: no untagged column names look sensitive.
ColumnSuggested tagConfidenceWhy

See exactly what a user would run for a query: the rewritten SQL and which columns are masked. Nothing is executed.

Values and SQL text are never stored, only tables, columns and policy names.

Connections

          
A saved login for a server that pipelines read from. The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again; pipelines only refer to the connection by name.

NameTypeTargetSecretActions

Every connect is checked against this fingerprint, so a changed or impersonated server is refused. Compare it with the one your SFTP provider publishes before pinning.

        


        

          

            
Apache Kafka, Redpanda, Confluent Cloud, MSK... Confluent-compatible registry (Confluent, Redpanda, Karapace, Apicurio compat API). Streams

          
Continuous, exactly-once ingestion of a Kafka / Redpanda topic into a Delta table in micro-batches. Unparsable messages go to a _dlq table next to it.

        

        
      


      

        

        
No streams yet. Create a Kafka connection first (Connections), then a stream.

        

          
StreamTopicTarget tableStatusRowsLagLast batchActions

          
            
          
        

      


      

        

        
Read the topic again from an earlier position (or skip ahead). The recorded offsets live in the Delta table, so this writes a Delta commit; with replace the rows that will be read again are deleted in the same commit, so nothing is duplicated.

        
Change what the stream reads or where it writes. Another connection to the same cluster and another table keep the position; another topic or cluster starts at the position you choose.


        

          

          

          

          

        


        

          

            

          

          

          

            

        


        

          
          
          
        

        

        

          

          
Rows already loaded stay, so the messages read again will be duplicated.

Columns come from the first batch (numbers, text, true/false; nested objects are kept as JSON text). Later messages are cast to the table; a field that does not fit or is new goes to _rescued_data unless "Add new fields" is on. _key, _topic, _partition, _offset, _timestamp are added to every row. Connection, topic and target cannot be changed after creation (the stored offsets belong to them).

A volume folder (/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>) or an S3 / S3-compatible location (s3://bucket/prefix/).

        


        

          
          
          
S3 sources are polled: pick an interval of 30 seconds or more (each poll lists the prefix) or a cron schedule. New objects are read in place, without downloading them; a malformed object is copied under _quarantine/ and removed if the key may delete it.

        


        

          

            
            
            
          

          

            
            
          

        


        

          
          
          
The pipeline starts the moment a file is fully written or renamed into the folder (a half-written file is never loaded). The rescan only catches what events can miss, such as network filesystems. Without Linux inotify it falls back to polling automatically.

        


        

          
          
          

            
          

          
The pipeline scans its volume only when a cron tick has elapsed. Missed ticks run once on catch-up.

Shallow clone

        
      

      
Creates a new table from  without copying any data: the clone shares the source's data files, so it costs no extra storage until it changes, and it stays valid even if the source is later vacuumed or dropped.
